positive: CONVERT THE GARMENT TYPE (highest priority) — whatever garment the wearer has on in the source, the result must be exactly this garment: hoodie with a natural hood, drawstrings, long sleeves, ribbed cuffs and a ribbed hem, and sweatshirt fabric. Rebuild it inside the scene instead of recolouring what is there: if the source shows a plain folded cuff or a straight plain hem, replace them with real 1x1 rib-knit cuffs and a rib-knit hem band, slightly narrower than the sleeve and body. The garment's fabric must match IMAGE 2 (mid-weight brushed fleece with rib-knit trims) rather than the source, and none of these may appear on it: no short sleeves, no rolled-up sleeves. Only the printed artwork, the wearer, the scene and any text overlays are preserved. The sleeves must be full length, reaching the wrist. GARMENT TYPE LOCK — the finished garment must be hoodie with a natural hood, drawstrings, long sleeves, ribbed cuffs and a ribbed hem, and sweatshirt fabric. Keep it that exact garment type in every pixel: no short sleeves, no rolled-up sleeves. The printed artwork, its placement and the scene stay as instructed, but the garment itself must never drift into another style. SLEEVE LENGTH — FULL-LENGTH LONG SLEEVES: each sleeve must run unbroken from the shoulder down to the wrist and cover the forearm completely. If the source photo shows a short-sleeve tee, lengthen the sleeves so they reach the wrist and end there. Do not leave short sleeves, do not roll or push the sleeves up, do not create three-quarter or elbow-length sleeves, and do not leave a bare forearm where the garment should be covering it. CUFF & HEM CONSTRUCTION — this is a sweatshirt / fleece top, so the sleeve ends and the bottom hem are real rib-knit (1x1 rib) bands with clearly visible vertical ribs, slightly narrower than the sleeve and body, joined to the garment with a seam, exactly as on a sweatshirt. The neckline is a ribbed crew neckband. Do not replace them with plain raw folded edges. HOOD DRAWSTRING — fixed design, identical on every colourway. (1) COLOUR: the whole length of both cords is the SAME colour as THIS hoodie's fabric — white hoodie gets white cords, black gets black, charcoal gets charcoal, grey gets grey, navy gets navy, sage gets sage; exactly that colour, not a tone lighter or darker. The cords are made from the garment's own fabric. (2) TIPS: each cord ends in a SHORT SILVER METAL AGLET — a small polished silver metal end cap, exactly one per cord, both tips silver and the same size. (3) TWINS: the two cords are identical twins — same colour, same thickness, same length, same silver tip — hanging symmetrically out of the two eyelets and starting at the same height. The cords in the source photo belong to the OLD colourway of that photo: replace their colour with this colourway's fabric colour, never copy it. Never one cord lighter than the other; never a frayed, tasselled, knotted or tufted end; never stone, marble, burlap or thick-rope texture.
negative: Do not produce short sleeves, half sleeves, three-quarter sleeves, rolled-up sleeves or an exposed forearm; the sleeves must reach the wrists. Do not replace the ribbed cuffs or ribbed hem with plain folded raw edges, do not add an elastic or gathered cuff, do not turn the ribbed hem into a straight cut hem. Do not add short sleeves, rolled-up sleeves. Do not colour the cord body anything other than this garment's own fabric colour; do not keep the source photo's cord colour (no white cords on a dark hoodie, no charcoal cords on a light hoodie); do not borrow another colourway's cord colour; do not make the two cords differ in colour, thickness, length or tip; do not draw frayed, tasselled, knotted or tufted cord ends; do not texture the cords like stone, marble, burlap or thick rope; do not use gold, brass, black or gunmetal tips — the tips are plain polished SILVER metal; do not make the whole cord metallic (only the two bottom tips are silver); do not remove the cords, the eyelets or the hood.
